text.p: The following is a direct contribution from commodity statistician F.O. Licht in Ratzeburg, Germany. Please address any queries to Helmut Ahlfeld on +00 49 4541 88920.

Robusta futures in London closed weaker across the board with most attention centered on the volatile session in New York. July and September were down $10 to close at $1,755 and $1,785 per tonne respectively. Traders were reluctant to set any new positions before the US Department of Agriculture's (USDA) crop estimates which were due after New York's close. The market expected USDA's forecast for Brazil for 1997/98 to surpass the working estimate of the Brazilian government of around 22 million bags and floated a figure of 27 million bags.

Arabica futures in New York closed lower across the board pressured by speculative long liquidation amid talk that USDA's world production estimate for 1997/98 would be bearish. Early estimates from the trade in Brazil have put next season's crop at anywhere from 18 to 25 million 60-kg bags, compared with this year's figure of at least 27 million bags. As a result July lost 12.10 cents/lb to close at 195.70 cents/lb, while September gave up 9.65 cents/lb to close at 182.75 cents/lb. Traders said that Colombian differentials continued to soften on the New York physical coffee market this week, despite CSCE future's recent sharp setback. It was added that roasters do not need nearby coffee. The decline began after finance minister Jose Antonio Ocampo announced the country was opening 'unlimited' coffee July/August registrations. Ocampo said the country was expected to export 2.5 million 60-kg bags of coffee, although traders said that this is too high a figure. FUNDAMENTALS

USDA - The United States Department of Agriculture in its bi-annual World Agriculture Production Report estimated 1997/98 (crop years) world green coffee production at 103.7 million bags, up from 100.7 million bags the previous season. USDA forecast the 1997/98 crop from top-grower Brazil would come in at 28 million bags compared with a revised 27.5 million bags in 1996/97. This estimate came as something of a shock as most analysts had agreed, that the 1997/98 crop would be lower than the 1996/97 harvest due to the two-year 'on-off' cycle which sees a smaller crop every other year. The Brazilian government had said that it is working with a figure of around 22 million bags for 1997/98, while traders are generally within a 23 to 25 million bag range. USDA pegged the 1997/98 Colombian crop at 11.3 million bags, versus a downwardly revised 1996/97 crop of 10.3 million bags, above official estimates of 10.1 million bags and trade estimates of below 10 million bags. UNITED STATES - US coffee roastings totalled about 350,000 60-kg bags during the week ended June 7 even with the previous week's total and compared to 345,000 bags in the corresponding week a year ago, Complete Coffee Coverage said. Cumulative roastings totalled 7.690 million bags versus 7.510 million bags in the same year ago period.

RUSSIA - Russia imported 188,400 bags of coffee in April 1997, roughly the same what was imported the previous month. That brought total imports since the beginning of 1997 up to 499,500 bags. Russia imports most of its coffee in the form of solubles. Soluble imports in January/April 1997 reached 430,600 bags green bean of which 159,200 bags were imported from India and 63,000 bags from Brazil.
F.O. LICHT - Our second estimate of the world coffee balance 1996/97 will be released on Tuesday, June 17, 1997, 14.00 hrs central European time.
